newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says Italy rail unaffected by chief's arrest.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy rail unaffected by chief's arrest.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday that the arrest of the managing director of Italy's state railway, Lorenzo Necci, would not affect the company's operations.
Necci, who has been overseeing the planned building of a multi-billion dollar high-speed railway across Italy, was arrested on Sunday in a corruption probe.
"The activity of the company will not suffer any interruption or any delay," Prodi told Italian reporters in Valencia, Spain, where he was attending an Italian-Spanish summit.
He said the board of directors of the company, Ferrovie dello Stato, would meet after Necci was questioned by magistrates in La Spezia, northwest Italy, on Wednesday.
Magistrates said on Monday that Necci had been held for questioning on suspicion of offences including criminal association, abuse of office, corruption, false accounting, fraud and embezzlement.
